note: Coverage plan for the independent human-labelled set of the semantic reader (EX-01, phase two). It states WHICH situations the authors must write, never a sentence, a label or an expected output. The families come from the failure families found in the development work (docs/research/recall_improvement_stage2.md, docs/research/failure_attribution.md); the dev, test and test2 sets informed them, so the set has to be written by people who have not seen those sets, the prompts, the model's answers or any label. Phase two measures SEMANTIC INTERPRETATION FROM TEXT independently of speech-recognition quality: every item is clean written text; the real-ASR family F17 has quota 0 here.

families.name: ordinary_paraphrase
families.what: The trainee performs one ordinary act of the taxonomy now, in plain but unfamiliar wording (not the textbook phrasing). Cover many different acts.
families.weight_reason: largest ordinary-act family; many different acts

families.name: indirect_natural_speech
families.what: An ordinary act performed in natural, indirect or elliptical speech (no keyword of the act, relying on the situation or on how people actually talk).

families.name: question_vs_assertion
families.what: Pairs of wordings that differ in being a question or a statement about the same content, where the approved definitions say whether the act is performed (for example an act that is performed by asking, against one that is performed by stating).

families.name: request_vs_completion_claim
families.what: A request or instruction to do something against a claim that it has been done, about the same thing.

families.name: hypothetical
families.what: The act is imagined, conditional or supposed, not performed.

families.name: reported_speech
families.what: Someone else's act or words are reported (a colleague, the patient, a chart); the trainee does not perform the act themself.

families.name: negation
families.what: The act is denied or refused, or something is not done.

families.name: actor_recipient
families.what: Who speaks, who does the act and to whom it is addressed differ (the patient or a colleague speaks; the trainee speaks to someone other than the usual recipient; an act is assigned to another person).

families.name: escalation_recommendation_handover_wording
families.what: Requests for a senior or other person to attend, review or decide, recommendations, and handover statements, in many wordings, with and without a named recipient. Authors state the recipient and the step in the scenario.
families.weight_reason: historically ambiguous (escalation against recommendation against handover wording) and safety-sensitive

families.name: emotion_acknowledged_vs_reassured
families.what: Speech about the patient's worry or fear: some acknowledges the feeling, some offers comfort or a prediction, some does both.

families.name: explain_action_vs_explain_procedure
families.what: Explaining what the trainee is about to do to the patient now, against explaining the course of the procedure or what will happen overall.

families.name: answer_with_patient_question_context
families.what: Replies whose act can only be recognised from the patient's question in the earlier turns (the scene has a patient question still waiting). Give prior_turns and set patient_question_pending to yes.

families.name: closed_loop_readback_context
families.what: Read-backs and confirmations of a colleague's instruction or result, recognisable only from the earlier turns (a critical result or order is waiting to be read back). Give prior_turns and set readback_pending to yes.

families.name: critical_topic_discussion
families.what: Speech about identity checks, allergy, consent, fasting state, a deteriorating sign or a structured handover: questions, statements, requests, in many wordings including ones that sound like an ordinary act. These are semantically labelled as they are; they are never credited from speech.
families.weight_reason: safety-sensitive: critical-topic discussion must never become critical-action credit

families.name: adversarial_or_misleading_wording
families.what: Wording built to look like a performed act without being one, or to mislead a reader (instructions addressed to the reader, claims about what was done, quoting, sarcasm, unfinished sentences, fillers).

families.name: out_of_window_valid_speech
families.what: An ordinary act that is semantically performed but spoken at a scenario step where the approved behaviour windows (content/assessment/mapping.json) do not list it. The author states the step; the engine, not the label, decides eligibility.

families.name: asr_evidence
families.what: OUT OF SCOPE for the first EX-01 evaluation (quota 0, not allowed). Real speech-recognition wording will be evaluated in a separate later phase from actual recordings and transcripts (audio and headset work, DC-08, EX-18, docs/testing/asr_safety_evaluation.md). Invented typos, swapped letters or glued words are never allowed anywhere in the set.

item_rules.scenario_step: a workflow step number 1 to 15 of content/assessment/mapping.json
item_rules.prior_turns: up to four earlier turns written as speaker: text separated by ' | ' (speaker is trainee, patient, colleague or tutor); empty if none
item_rules.speaker_role: who speaks the target utterance: trainee, patient, colleague or tutor
item_rules.patient_question_pending: yes only if the scene has a patient question still waiting for an answer
item_rules.readback_pending: yes only if a critical result or instruction is waiting to be read back
item_rules.author_intended_acts: the author's intention, used ONLY to check the coverage and the out-of-window family; it is never shown to an annotator and is never the label
item_rules.no_clinical_inventions: Use only the approved action definitions (content/assessment/taxonomy.json) and the scenario rules (content/assessment/mapping.json). Do not state a clinical requirement, a dose or a threshold.
item_rules.author_code: a short code for the author (A1, A2, ...) held in the roles record; never a name; never shown to an annotator
item_rules.asr_source: must be empty in phase two (no real-ASR family)
item_rules.near_duplicates: a sentence that is identical to, or a near-copy of, a sentence of any repository benchmark is refused by the owner's check; the check never shows the repository sentence to the author
